questions.q: What four tables does Project 1's parameterized query join?
options: SalesOrderHeader, SalesOrderDetail, Product, Customer
Customer, Employee, Store, Territory
SalesOrderHeader, Product, ProductCategory, Vendor
SalesOrderDetail, Product, Store, SalesTerritory
questions.explain: The query joins Sales.SalesOrderHeader, Sales.SalesOrderDetail, Production.Product, and Sales.Customer, scoped by territory and date range.

questions.q: What does action 0 (no hint) represent in this project's action space?
options: An invalid action that always returns a negative reward
Forcing the optimizer to use a hash join
Deferring to SQL Server's own default execution plan
Skipping the episode entirely
questions.explain: Action 0 appends no hint at all, letting the optimizer choose its own plan — and that plan becomes the baseline the reward is measured against in Lesson 6.

questions.q: What two features make up the agent's observation?
options: The query's estimated cost and actual row count
date_range_days and a territory-size proxy (customer count)
The chosen hint and the previous episode's reward
CPU time and logical reads from the last query
questions.explain: The observation is a small two-feature vector: normalized date_range_days and a normalized customer-count proxy for territory size.

questions.q: Why is this project's episode structure closer to a contextual bandit than a multi-step RL trajectory?
options: Because SQL Server does not support multi-step queries
Because each episode is exactly one decision with no delayed, sequential outcome
Because PPO cannot handle multi-step environments
Because the action space only has one valid action
questions.explain: Each episode samples a context, takes one action, and ends — there's no sequence of actions building toward a delayed outcome, which is the bandit shape.

questions.q: Why does this project still frame the problem as RL via Gymnasium and PPO rather than as a plain bandit algorithm?
options: PPO requires at least two steps per episode to function
It matches the rest of the lab's framing, and PPO handles a single-step episode without modification since a bandit is a special case of an RL problem
Gymnasium cannot represent bandit problems at all
SQL Server only accepts commands from a Gymnasium Env
questions.explain: The lesson frames this as a deliberate consistency choice: a contextual bandit is a special case of an RL problem, and Project 3 elsewhere in the lab is also RL, so the same tools apply cleanly.
